hypothesis: Dual-Space Decorrelation (applying Barlow Twins cross-correlation regularization directly to backbone features f alongside projection vectors p) prevents rank collapse in intermediate representations and maximizes backbone feature entropy, significantly improving linear evaluation accuracy compared to regularizing projections alone.
rationale: In previous iterations (iter 16 val_acc=0.6200), Barlow Twins decorrelation was applied solely to projection outputs z at the end of a non-linear 3-layer MLP. Because the projection head is non-linear, decorrelation in projection space does not prevent channel redundancy or feature collapse in the 768-dim backbone features f on which linear evaluation is actually performed. By packing backbone features f (768-dim) and projection outputs p (1280-dim) into the 2048-d output vector, the loss module can directly compute Barlow Twins feature decorrelation on both spaces, forcing every channel in the 768-dim backbone representation to capture non-redundant semantic information across views.
expected_effect: Direct backbone feature decorrelation will enforce channel orthogonality in feature space f, raising linear evaluation top-1 accuracy beyond the current 0.6200 record.
change_summary:
1. Updated BarlowTwinsModel to concatenate 768-dim backbone features and 1280-dim projection head outputs into a 2048-dim projection vector.
2. Upgraded BarlowTwinsLoss to Dual-Space Decorrelation Loss: computes Decoupled Contrastive Loss (DCL, tau=0.10) and Barlow Twins decorrelation on projection vectors p (1280-dim), plus direct Barlow Twins decorrelation on backbone features f (768-dim).
3. Retained the best-performing anti-aliased ResNet-26 backbone (1.5x width, 768-dim) and detail-preserving CIFAR-100 augmentations.
